evidence: frontend/apps/reality-web/src/components/favorites/PriceAlerts.tsx:98,108 — handleMarkRead/handleMarkAllRead catch blocks log the raw mutation rejection via console.error('Failed to mark price alert read:', err) / console.error('Failed to mark all price alerts read:', err). The err originates from @ppt/reality-api-client hooks (useMarkFavoriteAlertRead/useMarkAllFavoriteAlertsRead, imported at lines 13-18), i.e. the generated api-client. The repo's own lib/safe-error.ts documents that api-client rejections embed the originating request (config.data/request/response.config.data) and MUST be routed through toSafeLogMessage(err) to avoid serializing secret-bearing request bodies into the console. Sibling reality-web surfaces already comply (FeedImport.tsx:520, CrmConnection.tsx:409, RealtorManagement.tsx:579 all use toSafeLogMessage(error)); these two call sites bypass it — a convention/leak-prevention regression on a user-facing path.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/components/comparison/ComparisonUrlHandler.tsx:43-47 — shared-comparison loader fetches `${getApiBase()}/api/v1/listings/${id}` and returns `response.json() as Promise<ListingSummary>`, an unchecked cast of untrusted-shape network data across an API boundary. The loaded objects are pushed into comparison state via addToComparison (line 70) and later dereferenced at render in ComparisonView (listing.title/price/photos). The sibling fetch of the SAME endpoint in app/[locale]/listings/[slug]/page.tsx:86 deliberately routes the body through parseListingDetail() because a 200 can carry a malformed/partial body; this path has no such guard, so a wrong-shaped body is stored and can crash the client-side comparison view. `id` is also interpolated into the URL unencoded (sourced from the ?ids= query param via compare/page.tsx:24).
